quickPrompts: What should I learn after React?
Am I ready for a frontend internship?
Which projects should I add to my portfolio?

defaultActions.title: Complete your profile
defaultActions.detail: Add your current level and internship date for more relevant advice.

defaultActions.title: Review your roadmap
defaultActions.detail: Mark completed topics so the advisor can focus on genuine skill gaps.

defaultActions.title: Prepare one question
defaultActions.detail: Ask about a specific skill, project, or internship goal to get an actionable answer.

responseSets.response: After React, focus on the skills that turn components into a complete product: routing and data fetching with Next.js, API integration, form validation, and deployment. Build one small app that uses all four before adding another library. Based on this demo profile, TypeScript and testing should come next—not a new UI framework.

actions.title: Build one Next.js feature
actions.detail: Add a validated form that reads and writes data through an API route.

actions.title: Add TypeScript gradually
actions.detail: Type component props and API responses in one existing React project.

actions.title: Ship the project
actions.detail: Deploy it and document setup, decisions, and limitations in the README.

responseSets.response: You are ready to start applying while you strengthen a few gaps. Your React foundation and two projects are enough for early conversations. Prioritize one deployed project with a polished README, JavaScript fundamentals you can explain aloud, and a one-page resume tailored to frontend internships. Do not wait until every roadmap item is complete.

actions.title: Run a project audit
actions.detail: Check the core flow, mobile layout, loading states, and README.

actions.title: Practice your walkthrough
actions.detail: Explain one project from problem to deployment in three minutes.

actions.title: Close one fundamentals gap
actions.detail: Review async JavaScript, APIs, and Git before your first interview.

responseSets.response: Add a project that looks like real product work rather than another tutorial clone. A strong option is an internship application tracker with authentication, filters, form validation, and a responsive dashboard. Show your decisions in a short case study and include a live demo, screenshots, and clear setup steps.

actions.title: Define the core flow
actions.detail: Start with add, update, filter, and track application status.

actions.title: Write a useful README
actions.detail: Document the problem, stack, setup, tradeoffs, and next improvements.

actions.title: Publish a case study
actions.detail: Explain the problem, your approach, and what you learned.

fallback.response: A practical next step is to choose one clear internship target, compare its requirements with your current roadmap, and close the smallest important gap through a project. Spend this week producing evidence of one skill—not collecting more tutorials. Then update your GitHub README so a reviewer can understand what you built and why.
